kpis.name: S&P 500
kpis.note: Broad equity risk-on/risk-off signal. High VIX or S&P drawdown signals demand risk for Southwire construction end markets.

kpis.name: Brent Crude
kpis.note: Energy costs affect Southwire manufacturing and logistics. Sustained Brent >$90 pressures freight and resin input costs.

kpis.name: Copper (LME)
kpis.note: Primary raw material. Copper content of wire drives COGS. Sustained elevation compresses margin unless hedged or repriced.

kpis.name: Aluminum (LME)
kpis.note: Key input for aluminum wire and cable. Price signals secondary cost pressure and hedge calendar triggers.

kpis.name: Freight (Drewry WCI)
kpis.note: Ocean freight index drives import costs on raw materials and packaging. WCI >$4K signals elevated supply chain risk.
kpis.change: Monitor Drewry WCI weekly for rate momentum

kpis.name: VIX
kpis.note: Equity market fear gauge. VIX >25 indicates risk-off environment; monitor customer demand signals and receivables.

kpis.name: Natural Gas
kpis.note: Energy input for manufacturing and logistics. Sustained elevation pressures margin. Drives residential heating demand indirectly.

kpis.name: Gold
kpis.note: Risk sentiment indicator. Gold >$3,000 with VIX elevation signals macro uncertainty that may dampen CapEx spending by customers.

wire.title: Paperwork, lines, hours on hold: There's a 'Time Tax' on Americans who need help most
wire.summary: Annie Lowrey explores the administrative burdens people face applying for government benefits. It's not just about wasted time: "When the government treats us like this, we don't trust it," she says.

wire.title: Lionel Messi says he's retiring from playing internationally for Argentina
wire.summary: He said he wrote his retirement letter after the World Cup final in July, but waited to publish it because his father was facing health issues that eventually claimed his life.

wire.title: Nepal's hesitance to accept foreign help for flood relief comes under scrutiny
wire.summary: A group of the country's private sector power producers says Nepali authorities lost crucial time in rescuing hundreds of people trapped in hydropower tunnels.

wire.title: U.S., Venezuela strike oil deal. And, the staggering hidden toll of U.S. heat deaths
wire.summary: The U.S. and Venezuela have entered into an oil deal. And, NPR spent two years tracking heat-related deaths and found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat more than the official counts show.

wire.title: Russia's jet-powered drones bring empty Kyiv supermarket shelves and rattle Ukrainians
wire.summary: Russian forces relentlessly battered Kyiv and cities in the region around the Ukrainian capital for a fifth straight day, leaving some supermarket shelves bare after repeated strikes on warehouses.

wire.title: Attacks flare between the U.S. and Iran after a monthlong pause
wire.summary: U.S. threats erupt into attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran retaliates against U.S. targets in the United Arab Emirates and Jordan in the first exchange of fire since July 29.

wire.title: Why too many women are prescribed antibiotics for UTIs they don't have
wire.summary: A recent study found that many women treated for recurrent UTIs didn't have UTIs at all. Instead, their symptoms were caused by hormonally driven inflammation and pelvic floor dysfunction.

wire.title: Hit shows from Edinburgh's Fringe festival are coming to America. Here are our top picks
wire.summary: The annual "anything goes" performing arts festival featured more than 4,200 performances this year. These are the ones we're still talking about.

wire.title: Singapore is scrambling to stabilize birth rates. Experts see lessons for the U.S.
wire.summary: Singapore has unveiled a national initiative built entirely around its collapsing birth rate. Some demographers say the plan includes policy ideas that could help American parents.

wire.title: The U.S.-Venezuela oil deal won't lower your gas prices. Here's what you need to know
wire.summary: The Trump administration announced a deal Friday to develop a vast amount of Venezuela's oil reserves, with the U.S. taking a majority stake. Energy experts say there are many reasons to be skeptical.

wire.title: Nepal rescuers blast hillside in search of hydropower workers as families wait anxiously
wire.summary: Rescuers have resorted to explosives as they struggle to reach trapped workers, as the flooding death toll reaches 939.

wire.title: US and Iran trade strikes for first time in weeks
wire.summary: The attack on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz - the first known US strike since late July - has killed two people and injured two others.

wire.title: Man arrested after Swiss rave shooting that killed woman
wire.summary: A 22-year-old Italian woman was killed and several injured at a techno rave in Aarau.

wire.title: The jury's options in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial
wire.summary: Jurors have five options before them as they decide the fate of the former nurse charged with killing her three children.

wire.title: 'She slipped out of my hand' - children missing after ferry sinks off northern Cyprus
wire.summary: Ayten and Hayri Bicer's two young children are among 20 missing in an incident that killed eight people.

wire.title: US singer D4vd's celebrity lawyers withdraw from murder case
wire.summary: The singer, 21, will be now represented by a public defender in the murder trial of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. He has pleaded not guilty.
